newsitem.title: USA: Mexico '97 GDP to fall below expectations - Fleming.
newsitem.headline: Mexico '97 GDP to fall below expectations - Fleming.

text.p: The March deceleration in Mexican industrial activity, along with near-term weakness in domestic demand, suggests Mexico's economy will grow more slowly in 1997 than investors appear to expect, a Robert Fleming Inc report said.

Mexican industrial output grew 4.2 percent in March 1997 versus March 1996, the Finance Ministry reported Wednesday. Economists in a Reuters poll had projected growth of 7.65 percent during the period.

"Monthly evolution of these indicators has been the major support for optimistic GDP (Gross Domestic Product) forecasts for 1997," said Omar Borla, chief Latin America economist at Fleming. "We believe that, in the absence of a recovery in domestic demand in the near term, GDP growth for the year will fall short of market expectations."
Mexican GDP should expand about 4.6 percent in 1997 against 5.5 percent in 1996, Borla said. That compares with a market consensus 1997 growth estimate of between 5.1 and 5.5 percent, he said.
"People are getting too hyped about Mexico, expecting growth of 5.0 or 6.0 percent," Borla said. "There is no way, with the low investment participation in terms of GDP that the country has."
